assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: **partial** -- muse has a real, code-confirmed mechanism for
durably recording *which credential tier* backs a session -- a `payment_tier`
field whose enum literally includes the value `"subscription"` alongside
`stored_api_key`/`unsaved_api_key`/`env_api_key` -- but it only fires as a
byproduct of a payment/usage **gate** activating (a "fresh gated activation"),
not automatically on every ordinary turn the way Claude Code's statusline
ticks. A comfortably-subscribed account running normal turns is never
expected to trip this gate, so for the scenario's literal shape ("one
moderate turn" -> signal present) the answer is honestly partial, not yes.

daemon_capability: **unknown** -- the muse parser (`parser.go`) has zero
handling today for any of `payment_gate.*` / `subscription_entrypoint.*` (grep
confirms 0 hits), so nothing is built. But calling this `incapable` would
repeat the exact false-negative mistake #1960's shared context warns against
-- I have direct, primary-source evidence (the compiled binary's own embedded
Rust doc-comments and struct/enum definitions) that a durable, named,
non-inferred subscription/credential-tier field exists in the wire format.
What is NOT yet confirmed is whether `session.payment_gate.banner_shown`
itself is ever actually written to `session.jsonl` in practice (only its
sibling `session.subscription_entrypoint.impression` has been directly
observed on disk, twice, across two independent research passes). `unknown`
is the honest, calibrated call pending that direct confirmation.

driver_capability: **n/a** (frozen; no recipe/recording yet).

Route: **frozen** -- but for a narrow, evidence-anchored reason with a
concrete re-assessment trigger, not a blanket "no adapter" dismissal.

## New finding this pass surfaces (goes beyond muse-capabilities.md's existing
`subscription_signal` writeup)

The prior wave's `subscription_signal` research (muse-capabilities.md, 5.6
section) live-probed only `/upgrade` and `/status`, and concluded there is
"one confirmed durable subscription-related payload type"
(`subscription_entrypoint_impression`) whose *actual tier/plan value* was
never seen. That undersold what is actually in the binary. A direct
`strings`/context scan of the real, version-pinned binary
(`/Users/ingo/.local/bin/muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1`, resolved via the `muse`
launcher shim's `active_binary` lookup) surfaces THREE sibling
`SessionRuntimeEvent` variants in the same enum family, all serialized under
the `session.` prefix (the same durable-to-session.jsonl namespace as
`session.subscription_entrypoint.impression`, `session.started`,
`session.ended`, etc.):

- `session.payment_gate.banner_shown` -> `PaymentBannerShownRecord { session_id,
  model, payment_tier, has_action_url }`. Embedded doc comment: "TUI soft-gate
  fold on fresh gated activation, #8200/#10703 ... the gate-entry counter #8200
  aggregates by model + payment tier." `payment_tier`'s doc comment: "Credential
  tier at gate entry (#8200 dimension)" with enum values `subscription`,
  `stored_api_key`, `unsaved_api_key`, `env_api_key` -- literally, durably,
  muse stating its own billing/credential tier, not something inferred from a
  model name.
- `session.payment_gate.unresolved_at_poll_cap` -> `PaymentUnresolvedAtPollCapRecord
  { remint_attempts }`. Doc: "TUI bounded re-mint poll reaching cap still
  gated ... the bounded re-mint poll window elapsed still gated and went
  dormant ... the unresolved-outcome counter #8200 aggregates by model +
  payment tier." This is a genuine periodic POLL mechanism (a "two-phase poll
  schedule") checking billing/credential state -- the closest analog muse has
  to Claude Code's statusline tick, though it is conditioned on already being
  gated, not free-running on every turn.
- `session.subscription_entrypoint.impression` -> already confirmed durable
  (see below); doc comment additionally reveals its `surface` enum includes
  `upgrade_command`, `login_flow`, `spend_nudge`, `payment_banner`, and
  `quota_hit` (plus a retired `subscription_command` value) -- i.e. `quota_hit`
  is a real, named muse concept in code, which is new information relevant to
  the sibling 2.9 `token-quota-exhausted` / 5.7 `quota-burndown` cells (both
  currently left UNVERIFIED/undeclared in muse-capabilities.md as "inherently
  hard to trigger" -- this confirms the mechanism is real, not merely
  plausible, though still hard to trigger deliberately; not actioned here,
  out of this cell's scope).

Independently, a fresh grep of the local session corpus for
`payment_gate|subscription_entrypoint|payment_tier|quota_hit` found exactly one
hit, in a REAL, already-on-disk transcript
(`~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/01a09ed0-752c-75e1-b223-c5bd24e17876/session.jsonl`,
line 16): a `session.subscription_entrypoint.impression` record with
`surface:"upgrade_command"`, `entrypoint:"cli"` -- the same shape the prior
wave found via live `/upgrade` probe. This confirms the `session.*` family IS
written to disk for at least one sibling, but `payment_gate.banner_shown`
itself has never been directly observed on disk by either research pass.

## Why this stays frozen rather than routing to `record`

1. **No automatic per-turn trigger.** Claude Code's statusline ticks on a
   timer regardless of account state; muse's payment-gate family only fires
   when a "fresh gated activation" occurs -- i.e. typically when a
   pay-as-you-go/API-key account approaches or hits a spend boundary. A
   subscribed account running one ordinary turn is not expected to trip it at
   all, so the scenario's literal recipe ("one turn, then wait for the
   signal") does not reliably produce the signal on most accounts.
2. **No CLI mechanism to force the gate for testing.** `muse --help` / `muse
   exec --help` (checked live, this pass) expose no debug/force-gate flag; the
   condition is provider-account-state-dependent, the same shape the prior
   wave already flagged for `quota_exhaustion` ("inherently hard to trigger
   deliberately").
3. **`payment_gate.banner_shown` itself has never been directly observed on
   disk.** The evidence for its existence and shape is the compiled binary's
   own embedded type/doc strings (strong, but one level short of the
   `events.jsonl` citation bar `daemon=bug` requires) plus its sibling's
   confirmed durability in the same enum family (a reasonable but not
   certain inference -- shared enum, shared `session.` naming convention,
   shared serialization path).
4. **The scenario's acceptance criteria are Claude-Code/Codex-shaped.**
   `RateLimitSnapshot.Windows[].UsedPercent` (`core/domain/session/rate_limit.go`)
   is explicitly documented as "Codex's schema is the superset; Claude Code's
   statusline JSON is a strict subset" -- a windowed/percent-utilization model
   muse has no analog of anywhere (0 hits for `rate_limit`/`window`/
   `UsedPercent`-shaped fields in this pass's binary scan, consistent with the
   prior corpus scan's 0 hits for `rate_limit`/`quota`/`overloaded` literals).
   Even a fully-confirmed `payment_tier` signal would map only loosely onto
   `PlanType` (a single categorical value, no `Windows`/percent data at all),
   which is itself a design decision for whoever builds this, not a
   parser bug to fix.

## Re-assessment trigger (concrete, not vague)

Re-assess (or better, let a future `record` pass live-probe directly) once
either:
(a) a `session.payment_gate.banner_shown` record is directly observed in a
real `session.jsonl` (deliberately reach a payment/usage-gate state on an
account with a known credential tier and grep for it), or
(b) muse ships a documented, non-gated way to read back credential/payment
tier (e.g. a `muse status --json` or similar machine-readable surface distinct
from the TUI-only `/status` panel).
At that point the daemon-side work is a genuinely buildable parser branch
(new `payment_tier` -> a muse-native subscription-signal domain concept,
analogous to but not identical to `RateLimitSnapshot`), not an
architectural block.
caveats: VACUOUS-PASS CONDITION: a spec that merely asserts "some session.jsonl record exists after a normal turn" would pass trivially and prove nothing about subscription detection. Any future spec for this cell MUST specifically assert the presence of session.payment_gate.banner_shown (or .unresolved_at_poll_cap) carrying a payment_tier field -- and that record only appears when the test account is deliberately driven into a payment/usage-gate state, not on an ordinary comfortable-quota turn.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTY: whether this cell can ever be recorded depends on the test account's billing state at record time. A subscription account comfortably within quota, or a fresh pay-as-you-go account far from any spend boundary, will most likely NEVER emit payment_gate.banner_shown -- this is the same 'inherently hard to trigger deliberately' shape muse-capabilities.md already flagged for quota_exhaustion (2.9). Whoever attempts a future record pass needs an account state near a real spend/usage boundary, which cannot be manufactured from a flag.

DO NOT infer subscription status from muse-spark-1.3-contributor's model name or from auth.json's providers.meta.mechanism field. Checked this session: mechanism="oauth" on this host (account-login auth), yet the prior wave's own /status probe on an oauth-authenticated test account showed "No active subscription -- you're on pay-as-you-go". oauth-vs-api-key authentication METHOD and subscription STATUS are independent axes; muse login --help itself distinguishes them ("Log in with your Meta account to use a subscription (subscriptions don't apply to manually entered API keys)" -- confirmed live this session, muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1 strings dump). Only payment_tier (or an equivalent explicit field) is a legitimate, non-guessing signal.

auth.json (~/.config/muse/auth.json, field names only, no values copied per this task's instruction) carries no tier/plan/subscription field at all -- only schema_version and providers.meta.{mechanism, storage, obtained_via, api_base_url, user_full_name, user_email}. settings.json likewise carries none. Neither file is part of the daemon's current transport (muse adapter is FilesUnderRoot over session.jsonl only, per agent.go; no permission to read these files exists today) -- ruled out as an alternate discovery path, not merely unexplored.

model-catalog rows (~/.local/share/muse/model-catalog/*.json, checked this session) confirm the shared context's 'no dollar cost persisted' claim directly: all four rows including muse-spark-1.3-contributor carry cost: null. No billing-tier field exists per model row -- the only 'tier' field present (reasoning_effort_variants[].tier) is reasoning-effort strength (low/medium/high/...), unrelated to billing.

This assessment goes beyond muse-capabilities.md's existing subscription_signal writeup (which only covered /upgrade's impression event and concluded 'not confidently untraced'). The payment_gate/payment_tier family found here is new evidence for that document too, but updating it is out of this cell's scope -- flagging here so the finding isn't silently lost.

CROSS-REFERENCE WITH 5.7 (#2004): the sibling 5.7 quota-burndown cell (assessed the same wave, same binary) re-scanned for snake_case/Subscription-prefixed terms (SubscriptionUsageSnapshot, used_percent, window_duration_mins) and found real hits, where this cell's own search terms ('rate_limit', 'window', 'UsedPercent', PascalCase) found none. 5.7's own caveats note the gap is in THIS cell's search terms, not a correction to THIS cell's verdict: the hits 5.7 found belong to an unrelated subscription-usage-window concept (SubscriptionUsageSnapshot / window / weekly), never to payment_tier -- payment_tier is still daemon_capability:unknown on its own terms, unchanged by this. Recorded here (5.7 flagged it but declined to file it as a 5.6 correction) so the two cells stop reading as if they searched the same thing and disagreed: 5.6's daemon_capability:unknown is an open question about payment_tier specifically; 5.7's daemon_capability:incapable is a route/version-scoped finding about a different, unrelated field family (SubscriptionUsageSnapshot) at muse 1.2.1-R2847.1. Neither implies a verdict about the other, and neither implies muse has no account API (the subject of the separate prov(muse) ticket, #2007).

sources.note: Scenario's process/acceptance_criteria are explicitly Claude Code (statusline rate_limits POST) / Codex (PlanType) shaped; the api-key/absence variant is deliberately deferred to a separate subscription-detection-apikey cell (not this one).

RateLimitSnapshot doc comment: 'Codex's schema is the superset; Claude Code's statusline JSON is a strict subset ... Windows []RateLimitWindow ... PlanType ... Credits'. Confirms the target shape is provider-emitted windowed/percent data, which muse's payment_tier finding only loosely maps onto (a single categorical field, no Windows/percent).

'Muse exposes no documented native hook/callback mechanism ... the adapter is observe-only, the junie/aider shape: a single transcripts permission and no hooks.' Confirms there is no push-based statusline-tick analog; any subscription signal must arrive via session.jsonl tailing, not a hook.
grep -n -iE "payment|subscription|RateLimit|quota" -> 0 hits (checked this session). Confirms nothing is built for this signal today; genuinely unbuilt, not architecturally blocked.

Real version-pinned binary (resolved via the muse launcher shim's active_binary lookup, not the 33KB bash shim on PATH). Embedded Rust doc-comment + struct/enum strings: PaymentBannerShownRecord{session_id,model,payment_tier,has_action_url} with payment_tier enum {subscription,stored_api_key,unsaved_api_key,env_api_key} ('Credential tier at gate entry'); PaymentUnresolvedAtPollCapRecord{remint_attempts}; SubscriptionEntrypointImpressionRecord{surface,entrypoint} with surface enum including upgrade_command,login_flow,spend_nudge,payment_banner,quota_hit. All three payload_type strings (session.payment_gate.banner_shown, session.payment_gate.unresolved_at_poll_cap, session.subscription_entrypoint.impression) confirmed present as literal payload_type constants alongside other already-confirmed-durable session.* types.

Real on-disk record: {"payload_type":"session.subscription_entrypoint.impression","payload":{"kind":"subscription_entrypoint_impression","record":{"surface":"upgrade_command","entrypoint":"cli", ...}}}. Confirms the session.* payment/subscription family IS durably written for at least one sibling; payment_gate.banner_shown itself not yet directly observed.

Prior live /upgrade + /status probe: confirmed subscription_entrypoint_impression durable, /status TUI text 'No active subscription -- you're on pay-as-you-go' is ephemeral/non-durable (same class as /usage). Did not discover the payment_gate family (this pass's addition).

Prior corpus text scan (14-session sample): 0 hits for quota/rate_limit/overloaded/context_limit literals. Consistent with this pass's finding -- payment_gate/payment_tier don't contain those substrings, so that scan would not have caught them; not a contradiction, a scope gap in the substring list used.

'Log in with your Meta account to use a subscription (subscriptions don't apply to manually entered API keys). META_API_KEY always takes priority over the account login.' Confirms auth METHOD (oauth vs API key) and subscription STATUS are related but distinct axes -- the former is necessary-but-not-sufficient for the latter.

schema_version, providers.meta.{mechanism,storage,obtained_via,api_base_url,user_full_name,user_email}. mechanism="oauth" on this host. No tier/plan/subscription field. Not part of the daemon's current transport (no permission declared to read it).

cost: null for all 4 rows (muse-spark-1.2, 1.2-contributor, 1.3, 1.3-contributor); no billing-tier field per model row. Confirms shared context's 'muse-spark-* absent from pricing catalog' claim directly.

recipe.notes: applicable: false. No CLI mechanism forces muse's payment/usage gate (checked muse --help and muse exec --help live, this session -- no debug/force-gate flag exists), and the scenario's own recipe shape (one moderate turn + trailing sleep, per the Claude Code statusline template) will not reliably reach the gate on any account not already near a real spend/usage boundary. RE-ASSESS/RECORD WHEN either (a) a live account is deliberately driven into a payment-gate state and session.payment_gate.banner_shown is confirmed on disk with a payment_tier value, or (b) muse ships a non-gated, machine-readable way to read back credential/payment tier. At that point the daemon-side extension is a genuinely buildable parser branch mapping payment_tier onto a muse-native subscription-signal concept -- not an architectural block -- see this cell's body for the exact fields (PaymentBannerShownRecord/PaymentUnresolvedAtPollCapRecord) to wire up.
